meaning:
στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.)
[in LXX for צוֹק, etc. ;]
narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaphorical (Ken., Polyb., Deu.28:53, Wis.5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Rom.2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), 2Co.6:4 12:10.†
SYN.: θλίψις, q.v (AS)

elsewhere.note: oppression, and anguish on every soul of man who does evil, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
but in everything commending ourselves, as servants of God, in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
